from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Rate",
            ["Derivatives measure instantaneous change as a rate.", "Think of functions as input-output machines.", "Complex functions nest or multiply smaller ones."]
        )
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Derivatives measure instantaneous change as a rate.
        # Visualize tangent line slope (using #00FF00)
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.1 * x**3, x_range=[-2, 2], color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(curve, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        dot = Dot(color="#00FF00")
        dot.move_to(curve.point_from_proportion(0.5))
        
        tangent = always_redraw(lambda: TangentLine(curve, alpha=0.5, length=1.5, color="#00FF00"))
        
        self.add(curve, dot, tangent)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Think of functions as input-output machines.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # Load asset machine icon
        # [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/machine.svg]
        machine = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/machine.svg")
        self.place_at_grid(machine, "E3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        x_label = MathTex("x", color=WHITE).next_to(machine, LEFT)
        f_x_label = MathTex("f(x)", color=WHITE).next_to(machine, RIGHT)
        
        self.play(Write(machine), Write(x_label), Write(f_x_label))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Complex functions nest or multiply smaller ones.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")
        
        func1 = MathTex("f(g(x))", color="#FF00FF").scale(1.5)
        func2 = MathTex("f(x) \\cdot g(x)", color="#FF00FF").scale(1.5)
        
        self.place_at_grid(func1, "C5", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(FadeIn(func1))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(Transform(func1, func2))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Product Rule: The Collaborative Duo", [
            "Multiplying functions creates a growing area.",
            "Area change requires both sides changing.",
            "The Product Rule sums these two effects."
        ])
        
        # Load asset
        rect_svg = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/rectangle.svg")
        self.place_in_area(rect_svg, 'B2', 'D4', scale_factor=1.5)
        rect_svg.set_color("#FFFF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.play(FadeIn(rect_svg))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        # Animate change in area by changing width and height independently
        # Using ValueTracker to simulate growth
        w_tracker = ValueTracker(1.0)
        h_tracker = ValueTracker(1.0)
        rect_svg.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_width(w_tracker.get_value()).set_height(h_tracker.get_value()))
        
        self.play(
            w_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0),
            h_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(1)
        rect_svg.remove_updater(rect_svg.get_updaters()[0])

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        formula = MathTex(r"u'(x)v(x) + u(x)v'(x)", font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'E3')
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Chain Rule: The Nested Gears", [
            "Nested functions act like rotating gears.", 
            "Turning one gear moves the next one.", 
            "Multiply gear ratios for total speed."
        ])
        
        # Gear asset
        gear_path = "/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/gears.svg"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        gear1 = SVGMobject(gear_path, color="#FFA500")
        gear2 = SVGMobject(gear_path, color="#FFA500")
        gears = VGroup(gear1, gear2).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        self.place_in_area(gears, "B2", "C5", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(gears))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFA500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        gear1.set_color("#FF4500")
        gear2.set_color("#FF4500")
        
        # Animate gear rotation
        self.play(
            Rotate(gear1, angle=PI, rate_func=linear),
            Rotate(gear2, angle=-PI, rate_func=linear),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF4500")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        label1 = MathTex("f'(g(x))").set_color("#FFFFFF").scale(0.8)

        self.place_at_grid(label2, "E5")

        self.play(Write(label1), Write(label2))
        self.play(Indicate(product_label))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Conclusion & Summary", [
            "Product Rule: Derivative of u times v.", 
            "Chain Rule: Outer derivative times inner derivative.", 
            "Master these rules to model change."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        product_rule = MathTex(r"(uv)' = u'v + uv'").set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(product_rule, "B2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(product_rule))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        chain_rule = MathTex(r"(f(g))' = f'(g)g'").set_color("#FF4500")
        self.place_at_grid(chain_rule, "C2", scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Write(chain_rule))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FF4500"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Final summary graphic
        summary_group = VGroup(product_rule, chain_rule)
        checkmark = Checkmark = Text("✓", color="#FFFFFF").scale(2)
        self.place_at_grid(checkmark, "E3", scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(checkmark))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Mastering the Product and Chain Rules in Calculus

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Rate
sections.content: Briefly visualize the derivative as the 'speedometer' of a function. Introduce the concept of a function machine: an input x goes in, f(x) comes out. Emphasize that we are now looking at functions within functions (nested) and products of functions.
sections.example: An animation of a car's speed (derivative) changing as it travels along a winding road.

sections.title: The Product Rule: The Collaborative Duo
sections.content: When two functions, u(x) and v(x), are multiplied, the derivative isn't just the product of their derivatives. Use an area-model animation: a rectangle with sides u(x) and v(x) expanding. The change in area is the sum of two strips: u(x)dv + v(x)du.
sections.example: A cat running (function u) while carrying a toy that is growing in size (function v). The total 'growth' of the scene depends on both variables changing simultaneously.

sections.title: The Chain Rule: The Nested Gears
sections.content: Visualize the chain rule as a system of gears. If Gear A turns Gear B, and Gear B turns Gear C, the speed of C is the product of the gear ratios. Formula: d/dx[f(g(x))] = f'(g(x)) * g'(x).
sections.example: A mechanical robot arm: the shoulder rotation (outer function) affects the wrist position (inner function). To find the velocity of the hand, you multiply the angular change of the shoulder by the reach change of the arm.

sections.title: Interactive Synthesis: Putting it Together
sections.content: Demonstrate a complex function that requires both rules. Explain the 'Out-to-In' strategy: peel the layers like an onion (Chain Rule) and look for internal products (Product Rule).
sections.example: A rocket launch: the fuel consumption (inner) is multiplied by the altitude gain (outer). We calculate the total 'jerk' (acceleration change) using the product rule while applying the chain rule to the time-dependent fuel pressure.

sections.title: Conclusion & Summary
sections.content: Recap: Product Rule = 'uv' + 'vu' (derivative alternation). Chain Rule = 'Outside derivative' * 'Inside derivative'. Quick visual summary of the gear-and-rectangle animation.
sections.example: A final visual cheat-sheet showing the two formulas appearing on a screen like HUD data for the robot from Section 3.
